requirements.title: Introduction to Crime, Law, and the Justice System
Introduction to Crime, Law, and the Justice System rule
requirements.summary: What do we know about crime and justice? In these three courses, students have an opportunity to develop a foundational understanding of three related phenomena: why crime exists, how our criminal justice system responds to crime, and the constitutional and legal oversight of this process.

requirements.title: Current Crime and Justice Issues rule
requirements.summary: These courses introduce students to topical issues related to crime and justice.

requirements.title: Current Crime and Justice Issues course choice
Crime Problems and Criminal Justice Institutions
Crime Problems and Criminal Justice Institutions rule
requirements.summary: The 2000-level courses in this list ask how does justice work and for whom? These courses introduce students to the systems and institutions tasked with providing justice. Each includes experiential learning components in cooperation with local criminal justice institutions. The 3000-level courses in this list provide students with a deeper look at a range of crime problems.

requirements.title: Crime Problems and Criminal Justice Institutions course choice
Systemic Issues rule
requirements.summary: These courses consider systemic issues facing the criminal justice system.

requirements.title: Creating Knowledge About Crime and Justice
Creating Knowledge About Crime and Justice rule
requirements.summary: How do we know what we know about crime and justice—and how do we develop new knowledge? This course covers how to harness data to learn about issues, identify solutions, and advocate for change.

requirements.title: Criminal Justice Elective rule
requirements.summary: These courses round out our knowledge of crime and justice.

requirements.title: Criminal Justice Elective course choice
requirements.summary: Required: two additional criminal justice electives from the 3000, 4000, or 5000 level.

notes: Credits use the catalog’s stated semester hours. Bundle credits belong to requirement nodes; individual amounts are supplied only when independently stated by a course catalog. Unverified alternative-course amounts and variable-credit scalar amounts remain unknown.
Course categories are editorial. Source-stated outcomes are paraphrased program aims, not measured graduate outcomes.
The local curriculum is represented; the degree remains partial because full universitywide and conditional policy execution has not been established.

Official subject-catalog metadata checked for 34 courses; each course cites that source. Variable subject-catalog credit ranges remain null in scalar credits, while program-specific required credits remain on their requirement nodes.

Universitywide and NUpath criteria are now represented through verified shared policy bindings. The major-page reference notes describe what that page incorporates; linked policy rules appear separately in the resolved graph.

Open subject/level ranges, explicit grade/overlap limits and advisor-approved substitutions are represented criteria, not missing invented finite course lists. Individual approvals and registration eligibility remain governed by those rules.

NUpath is competency-based: approved attributes may be met through major or elective courses. This inventory does not fabricate all eligible class sections. BA-language, NYC-campus and nursing-specific general-education panels are not inherited by these Boston BS/BSEnvE degrees.

Permitted home-college options and their additional progression/graduation rules have not been exhaustively verified for this combined degree. Catalog hosting context is not assumed to fix the student’s designated home college.
